text:
ada: spotting ~90 Pending GPU pods in us-west1, skewed to us-west1-a. Looks like scheduler bias for anchored pool + strict nodeSelector on legacy jobs.

chris: paste of event for one pod: `FailedScheduling: 0/24 nodes are available: 10 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu, 9 node(s) didn't match nodeSelector, 5 node(s) had taints the pod didn't tolerate.`

mike: We rolled the anchored-pool scoring extender last month; it gives a +1000 hard bump for nodes in the anchored pool. It doesn't account for nodeSelector mismatches; hence pods get rejected then backlogged to a.

ada: Quick mitigation idea: mutate legacy tiny-gang pods to prefer any a100 shape instead of hard nodeSelector. Lower risk than disabling the extender.

chris: Proposed patch (canary): replace nodeSelector with preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution affinity preferring `gpu.shape=a100-small` but allowing `a100-medium`/`a100-large`. Will target ml-canary first.

infra-bot: queued patch job by ada: patch poddefaults/tiny-gang-default; CI run infra-patch-1767890123 link https://ci.redwood/patch/1767890123

mike: Also noticed warm-pool controller didn't scale because of a cooldown flag (ENG-INFRA-214). If warm pool had grown, less pressure on anchored pool. Add ENG-INFRA-214 to follow-ups.

ada: Canary applied; 6/8 pending pods scheduled across b/c within 90s. No latency anomalies in canary traces.

chris: Follow-ups: ENG-SCHED-420 to replace hard extender bump with soft bias that respects nodeSelector/affinity, ENG-INFRA-214 warm-pool cooldown fix, add alert for AZ occupancy skew >60%.

infra-bot: incident INF-1767890123 created; assignees ada,chris,mike.

ada: Closing; will update runbook with the temporary mutate command and thresholds to watch.
